newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Asian demand supports gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Asian demand supports gas oil.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up slightly late afternoon on Thursday despite weaker crude and gas oil futures on expections of regional demand, traders said.
"Gas oil is steady because there are strong belief among players that the market will rebound," one trader said.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.15/$25.35 per barrel down from Wednesday's $25.30/$25.40, but up 5 cents from midday brokers said.
The market opened to trade at $24.95 per barrel and later in the morning at $25.00, $25.05 and $25.10, they said. It traded in the afternoon at $25.20 per barrel.

The steady tone came despite March Brent crude losing 62 cents to close at $20.52 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange on Wednesday and March gas oil opening on Thursday down $4.50 per tonne to to 180.00.
It was last traded down $4.00 per tonne on the day at $180.50.

Traders said the Singapore market was holding its own on regional demand with unexpected buying seen from Thailand where refinery problems had forced refiners there to import two 30,000-tonne cargoes from Singapore for February arrival.
They were also optimistic of fresh demand from China after the Lunar New year holidays and recent exports of about 80,000-tonnes from Singapore to India and Bangladesh.
The jet fuel market remained under selling pressure as no new winter demand is emerging from North Asia. March jet fuel swap was quoted at $27.15/$27.40, down about 50 cents from Wednesday.

Fuel oil swaps were quoted down about $1.00 per tonne in line with the weaker crude market in quiet trade. March was last quoted at $99.50/$100.50 per tonne, from Wednesday's $101.00/$102.00 per tonne. It traded earlier today at $100.00
